editorial:
Imagine feeling so trapped by your own fear that the only place you feel safe is behind a computer screen. You will meet Jakob, a teenager who struggles with bad anxiety and hides from the world in virtual chat rooms. Everything changes when he meets Kristjan, an older man who seems to understand his pain. The movie starts off feeling like a slow burn, but it quickly turns into a strange and tense trip. It is not your typical horror movie with jump scares, but it creates a heavy mood that makes you feel the characters' sadness and loneliness as they try to bond over their shared trauma.

What really works here is the acting, as both leads make you believe in their broken relationship. The pacing is a bit slow at times, which might bore some of you, but it helps build the tension. If you like stories that mess with your head and explore dark emotions, you should definitely give this one a try. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the moody lighting. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great way to keep this unique story on your shelf.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a very dark and confusing note. Jakob and Kristjan's bond turns toxic as they push each other toward self-destruction. You see them spiraling deeper into their mental pain until the line between reality and their fantasies blurs. It finishes with a feeling of hopelessness, showing that they cannot truly save each other from their pasts. There is no happy ending here, just a sad look at how broken people can hurt one another.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and moody dramas about mental health.
